newsitem.title: JAPAN: Kampo says no plans to trim foreign bond purchases.
newsitem.headline: Kampo says no plans to trim foreign bond purchases.

text.p: Japan's Postal Life Insurance Bureau (Kampo) said on Thursday that it was not planning to trim its purchases of foreign bonds, given the interest rate differential between Japan and other countries such as the United States.

"We have not changed our basic understanding that the current fundamentals continue to be suitable for foreign bond investment," said an official at Kampo, which is regarded as one of the world's biggest investors.
"Obviously, we are not intending to cut back our foreign bond investment," he said.

The official said that even though Kampo has not announced specific investment plans for the 1997/98 fiscal year starting April, there is a possibility that the volume of foreign bond purchases could rise next year compared with 1996/97.
He said the interest rates of foreign bonds were generally more attractive than domestic interest rates.
However, Kampo is not planning to set a specific target level for foreign bond investment for its portfolio in 1997/98 because it cannot determine the foreign exchange rate trend in the long term.
"Of course, we set plans for a one- or two-month period, but we cannot disclose the plans because they could have a great impact on the market," the official said.
Kampo is planning to invest mainly in U.S. Treasuries and German bonds with various maturities, including long-term bonds, the official said.
"In the past, we have had about 5.9 percent of our total funds in foreign bonds," the official said, adding that the rate was about 3.9 percent at the end of January.
Kampo has been able to use currency forward transactions to hedge its holdings of foreign currency-denominated bonds since May 1995, following the revision of a law.
"We can hedge our holdings of foreign bonds anytime, but we are still in a process of studying the system," he said.
